\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Transitive symmetry]
\lean{FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005
}
\label{FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.permuteInput}
Let $\beta$ be a type and let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\beta$. The function is transitive
symmetric if, for every pair of coordinate indices $i,i'$, there is a permutation $\pi$
of the coordinates that sends $i$ to $i'$ and leaves $f$ unchanged on every input when
the input is permuted by $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry implies transitive symmetry]
\lean{FABL.IsSymmetric.isTransitiveSymmetric}
\label{FABL.IsSymmetric.isTransitiveSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $X={-1,1}^n$, and let $f:X\to\beta$ be invariant under every
permutation of its coordinates. Then for any two coordinates $i,i'\text{ in
}{0,ldots,n-1}$, there is a permutation $\text{ of the coordinates}$ sending $i$ to
$i'$ under which $f$ is invariant.
\end{theorem}

respect to the coordinatewise order: if $x_i\le y_i$ for every coordinate $i$, then

\end{theorem}

$x,y$ indexed by $n^d$ coordinates, if $x_i\le y_i$ at every coordinate, then recursive
majority of depth $d$ on $x$ is at most recursive majority of depth $d$ on $y$.
\end{theorem}

returns $1$ exactly when every coordinate is $1$ and returns $-1$ otherwise, is
monotone: if one input is at most another in every coordinate under the order $-1<1$,
then its output is at most the other's under the same order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transitive symmetry of the AND function]
\lean{FABL.andFunction_transitiveSymmetric}
\label{FABL.andFunction_transitiveSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric.isTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.andFunction, FABL.andFunction_symmetric}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every pair of coordinates $i,i'\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
there is a permutation of the coordinates sending $i$ to $i'$ under which the function
on $\{-1,1\}^n$ that outputs $-1$ when every coordinate is $-1$ and outputs $1$
otherwise is invariant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transitive symmetry of the OR function]
\lean{FABL.orFunction_transitiveSymmetric}
\label{FABL.orFunction_transitiveSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric.isTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.orFunction, FABL.orFunction_symmetric}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the OR function on sign vectors of length $n$, which
returns $1$ exactly when every coordinate is $1$ and returns $-1$ otherwise, is
invariant under coordinate permutations, and for any two coordinates there is such a
permutation sending the first coordinate to the second.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of tribes]
\lean{FABL.tribes_monotone}
\label{FABL.tribes_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.andFunction_monotone, FABL.orFunction_monotone, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{3}
For all nonnegative integers $w$ and $s$, the tribes function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $sw$ is monotone: if one input is coordinatewise at most another, then its
output is at most the other's, with the signs ordered by $-1<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Block coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.blockCoordinatePermutation}
\label{FABL.blockCoordinatePermutation}
\leanok
Let $s,w$ be natural numbers, and let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be permutations of
$\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$ and $\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$, respectively. Identify the $sw$ coordinates
with pairs $(i,j)$, where $i<s$ and $j<w$; the block coordinate permutation sends the
coordinate $(i,j)$ to $(\sigma(i),\tau(j))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Action of a block coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.blockCoordinatePermutation_apply}
\label{FABL.blockCoordinatePermutation_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.blockCoordinatePermutation}
\difficulty{1}
Let $s,w$ be natural numbers, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$, and
let $\tau$ be a permutation of $\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$. For every $i<s$ and $j<w$, the
permutation of the $sw$ coordinates induced by applying $\sigma$ and $\tau$ to the two
coordinates sends the coordinate corresponding to $(i,j)$ to the one corresponding to
$(\sigma(i),\tau(j))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes is not symmetric]
\lean{FABL.tribes_not_symmetric}
\label{FABL.tribes_not_symmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.andFunction, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.orFunction, FABL.permuteInput, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{6}
For integers $w,s$ with $1<w$ and $1<s$, the tribes function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $sw$ is not invariant under all permutations of its input coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Example2 9]
\lean{FABL.example2_9}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
